rows.claim: Published request and agency response; not an appropriation or solicitation.
rows.explanation: Throughout CD1, Queens the senior centers are older and require modernization post Covid 19. These facilities provide essential services to our older population. Kitchens in centers are antiquated. Floors in the centers require replacement and /or upgrading, Structures require maintenance and reimagining for multi-use. High speed technology installation and other items have been noted for during renovations throughout the districts centers. Our elder population relies on the services and as our senior population expands (post baby-boomer) these facilities are highly utilized in our district, As gen X and millennials grow older preparations need to be made for the extremely high rate of older New Yorkers to follow.
rows.headline: Renovate or upgrade a senior center
rows.response: Further study by the agency of this request is needed.

rows.claim: Published request and agency response; not an appropriation or solicitation.
rows.explanation: My Ride Program (Taxi Smart Card Pilot) Program expanded to for CD 1. We have requested for the opportunity for our residents to have the pilot in our district since the sunset of the Taxi Smart Card program with similar features. The program had no funding for advertising. It failed because of lack of use. Advertising is necessary for new programs to jump-start. We now have social media. This program allowed the elderly and disabled to have access to transportation in a real-world way. Individuals were able to access things such as doctor's appointments. Due to the limitations of other services this program was a quality-of-life asset. This program requires funding and expansion.
rows.headline: Increase transportation services capacity
rows.response: Further study by the agency of this request is needed.

rows.claim: Published request and agency response; not an appropriation or solicitation.
rows.explanation: As the Baby Boomer (61 million) generation matures and the Millennials (1.5 billion) are aging the adult population is magnifying. Funding for additional personnel in Senior Centers has become evident. The Boomers noted at one time to be the "largest" generation are now in need of elder services. Additional personnel in CD1Q to service this growing demographic is sorely needed to keep up with service provision. Preparation for the aging Millennials needs to be made approximately (44%) in population in a nyc.gov report for Astoria., Queens. We require senior centers for the vital services they provide.
